scope: Static source map of only the two named test files; no statement that these tests have been executed or passed in this review, and no claim that listed gaps are absent from other files.

fixture_and_seam_classification.classification: Concrete native FreeCAD document, Part box, ObjectsFem analysis/material/mesh and Fem.FemMesh with four sequentially numbered nodes and one tetrahedron. No mesher or CalculiX solve is used.

SimpleNamespace fea plus literal hand-authored V1 deck/request/output and a synthetic solver identity file that is never executed. Uses private _model_digest to create import metadata; this is import-boundary/model-identity coverage, not public export or solver accuracy qualification.

Concrete native FreeCAD box/one-tetra mesh and FemToolsCcx in test_mode. Input deck/request/metadata are hand-authored. engine creates a real executable Python subprocess fixture for policy queries and synthetic output bytes, not a CalculiX structural solve.

coverage.behavior: Real model edits invalidate previously acceptable import context
coverage.assertions: A control import first succeeds. Each subsequent real change must fail with model_digest mismatch and stale the control result: material dictionary, box shape, replaced native mesh coordinates/connectivity, ElementGroupReferences, gravity, contact stiffness/references, rigid-body ReferenceNode/prescribed mode, section References/AccountingBody and solver nonlinearity.
coverage.boundary: Native FreeCAD objects; fake import context, no public writer or child solve. The mesh changes replace the FemMesh, not an actual Gmsh remesh.

coverage.behavior: Deck/request/solver-byte freshness and exact requested filename
coverage.assertions: Changed deck, request or binary bytes reject import before output parsing. Dotted basename selects model.v1.inp and binds the resulting source to that exact deck rather than neighboring model.inp.
coverage.boundary: First is fake import metadata; second uses ordinary start_ccx with real synthetic executable subprocess, not writer-generated graph or native ID proof.

coverage.behavior: Public native material wrappers and container content identity
coverage.assertions: Retained wrapper reads must not change identity; changed quantity/float precision, lists, 2D/3D arrays/depth, appearance, description and physical-model membership must change private model digest and input fingerprint. Empty array dimensions, null versus authored zero and nonquantity float columns remain distinguishable; ambiguous physical/appearance properties reject.
coverage.boundary: Native material and mesh wrappers are concrete. Digest/fingerprint/property_value are private serialization seams, not a public export-cache lifecycle. Wrapper mutations are assigned back through material setters and ShapeMaterial.

coverage.behavior: Capability probes stay private and clean up on success or unsupported return
coverage.assertions: The unsupported real executable /usr/bin/false is rejected. The explicit boundary-mock test requires private non-project cwd, DEVNULL stdin, resolved executable path for absolute/relative/PATH references, and deletion of a simulated probe-job marker directory after either return0 or201.
coverage.boundary: Only subprocess.run is replaced in the cleanup test; CompletedProcess and marker file emulate external executable behavior. It does not test failed writer cleanup.

coverage.behavior: Public writer capacity refusal occurs before mesh work and normal export binds effective policy
coverage.assertions: The four-port unfinished/no-mesh model must refuse a three-record capacity with an empty export directory. Real whole write_inp_file on the one-tetra model records support1/port1/total2, object identity, binary SHA and request SHA and creates no accounting result. Malformed query mappings reject. An equilibrium cut without NativeForceAccounting refuses instead of stress fallback.
coverage.boundary: Public FemToolsCcx writer call is real in tests555 and625; only executable version/capacity subprocess.run responses are mocked. Test610 uses a SimpleNamespace writer; test698 directly calls capacity_preflight. No real native solver or full graph/native-ID parity is established.

coverage.behavior: Resource-policy freshness and owned-child capacity attestation
coverage.assertions: Changed budget requires rewrite before solver-entry marker or old FRD/accounting quarantine. Missing/wrong/duplicate/malformed owned-child applied-capacity echoes reject Current import. Legacy metadata without capacity still refuses the current too-small budget without altering old outputs.
coverage.boundary: Real synthetic executable query/run subprocesses through public start_ccx; environment budgets are patch.dict overrides. The request is hand-authored, not a production export fixture.

coverage.behavior: Fresh movement bytes, terminal run context and failure recovery
coverage.assertions: Missing fresh FRD is UNAVAILABLE and old bytes recoverable; exact fresh bytes bind requested state and model/deck/request/binary identities without qualifying displacement. Repeated finish_run cannot rebind replaced bytes. Child error7 and launch OSError preserve recoverable old FRD without Current result; symlink target is untouched; unfinished and legacy run contexts cannot attest movement.
coverage.boundary: Mostly real synthetic executable children through start_ccx or run_context/finish_run/import_result. Only the -i child Popen is replaced with OSError for launch-failure coverage. This is solver-run/output custody, not export-resolution-context cleanup.

coverage.assertions: Actual FreeCAD FCStd save/reopen retains exact AccountingData/resultants but restores Stale status. Default accounting/cut options remain opt-in. Native model change and explicit restored callback invalidate Current status.
coverage.boundary: Concrete FreeCAD persistence; imported forces and movement bytes are synthetic boundary fixtures, not native physical accuracy evidence.

honest_gaps_in_these_two_files: No test retains and reuses an export/mesh-resolution context across repeated public write_inp_file calls after reference edits, remesh or failure; accounting import/run context is a distinct seam.
No Placement edit, transformed/linked-part placement or placed-solid owner selection case.
No Analysis.Group reorder, remove/readd, mesh-group enumeration-order permutation or deterministic declaration-order assertion.
No sparse/noncontiguous native node or element IDs, renumbering, or preservation of old-to-new native ID allocation across fresh exports.
No test mutates a cached public list/dict/reference/group container in place and then proves a fresh export reads it; native material wrapper content tests are narrower serialization checks.
No real Gmsh remesh or native CalculiX solve; changed coordinate/connectivity tests construct replacement FemMesh objects and synthetic subprocesses are not physical qualification.

No mid-writer exception followed by retry proving export-context cleanup, no stale cross-analysis context reuse, and no public writer parity after a reference edit. Probe and solver-output cleanup tests do not substitute for this.
No performance bound, fixture equivalence, complete264-port/2113-declaration native-ID graph or physical equilibrium qualification in these two files.
